taxonomy.description: The source place, organization, event, or work belongs to or is located in the target country. Do not apply to a person; do not infer unstated geographic containment.
The source place is located in the target administrative territory. Require the document to state the containment; do not infer a transitive location chain.
The source organization has its headquarters in the target location. A branch office or activity in a place is not headquarters.
The source person was born in the target place. Residence, citizenship, death, or employment alone do not establish birthplace.
The source person died in the target place. Birthplace, residence, or burial alone do not establish place of death.
The target person is the father of the source person. Do not reverse parent and child or infer from shared surnames.
The target person is the mother of the source person. Do not reverse parent and child or infer from shared surnames.
The two people are or were married spouses, including explicitly stated former spouses. A proposed marriage or other association does not establish marriage. This relation is symmetric.
The target person is the child of the source person. Do not reverse the direction or infer from shared surnames.
The target person or organization founded or co-founded the source organization. A later owner, executive, or employee is not necessarily a founder.
The source asset, organization, or work is or was owned by the target entity. Operation, creation, employment, or partnership alone does not establish ownership.
The target organization or person publishes or published the source work. Creation, distribution, and publication are distinct.

chunks.title: Truth in Music Advertising
chunks.text:
The Truth in Music Advertising act or bill , also known as Truth in Music Performance Advertising or simply Truth in Music , is legislation , adopted into state law by most U.S. states , that aims to protect the trademark of musical recording artists .
The legislation provides that the name of a famous musical group can not be used by a group of performers unless they include at least one member of the original group .
The intent of the legislation is to prevent unfair or deceptive trade practices , and to protect the livelihood of musicians who were in famous musical groups .
The legislation , co - authored by former Sha Na Na member Jon " Bowzer " Bauman and promoted by him and Mary Wilson of the Supremes , was not passed by the U.S. Congress , but has been enacted in 34 of the 50 states .
The legislation has been tested in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit .
